Q446.reason: Voting regulations that impose only minimal burdens get rational-basis review under Anderson-Burdick, so an upheld law must be rationally related to a legitimate purpose; my earlier strict-scrutiny reasoning was wrong.

Q432.reason: Ballot-access burdens tied to candidacy are analyzed under due process as well as equal protection, and option A is the more plausible of the two team-noted answers, since C wrongly treats the state's sovereignty as a bar to federal review.

Q437.reason: A mass that vanishes after urethral catheterization is the classic sign of a distended bladder, so C's observation is right even though its attribution to an ovarian cyst is wrong; A is also flawed because pulsatile masses are not always aneurysms.
